stem: One plant is visibly wilted while adjacent plants on the same bench remain upright. What is the strongest interpretation at this stage?
choices: The finding is currently isolated; document it, compare additional representative locations, and avoid a broader causal conclusion until the pattern is established
Because adjacent plants are upright, the issue can be treated as plant-specific and no broader comparison is needed
The local contrast makes an irrigation-delivery problem the leading confirmed cause even before other locations are checked
The bench should be classified as affected because one confirmed abnormal plant is sufficient to define the bench-level pattern
rationale: The current evidence supports an isolated observation, not a room-, bench-, or cause-level conclusion. Additional representative comparison determines whether the finding remains isolated or belongs to a larger spatial pattern.
